This regulatory action coincides with broader efforts by the Trump administration to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips, closing regulatory loopholes that previously enabled Chinese firms to access powerful processors remotely. In response to these escalating restrictions, Alibaba leadership indicated a strategic shift toward utilizing domestic hardware, including the training of upcoming Qwen artificial intelligence models on proprietary T-Head chips designed entirely in-house.

stories.title: Babar Azam stars with brilliant half-century on ILT20 debut for Desert Vipers
stories.summary:
Babar Azam delivered an impressive performance during his debut appearance in the International League T20, guiding the Desert Vipers to a comfortable six-wicket victory over the Sharjah Warriorz. The match took place at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium during the second fixture of the tournament's 2026 season.

Asked to bat first, the Sharjah Warriorz constructed a competitive total of 166 runs for the loss of nine wickets in their full quota of 20 overs. Paul Walter anchored the Sharjah innings with an aggressive knock of 75 runs from 43 deliveries, keeping his team competitive despite regular wickets falling around him.

Chasing a target of 167 runs, the Desert Vipers completed the run chase with 15 balls to spare, finishing at 167-4 in 17.3 overs. Babar Azam played a commanding role in the pursuit, scoring an outstanding 86 runs off just 51 balls. His magnificent innings featured 13 boundaries and two towering sixes, establishing a dominant strike rate of 168.62 before he was eventually dismissed by Adam Milne.

Solid contributions from teammates supported the successful run chase. Joe Clarke chipped in with 35 runs from 27 deliveries, while Andries Gous added a quick-fire 13 runs from five balls. Late in the innings, Shimron Hetmyer and team captain Shadab Khan remained unbeaten on four and eight runs respectively, safely steering the Desert Vipers across the finish line to secure their opening win of the 2026 campaign.

stories.title: Punjab government launches QR code tracking system to streamline sanitation complaints
stories.summary:
The Punjab government has rolled out an innovative QR code-based system designed to register and resolve sanitation complaints across the province. Announced during a special review meeting led by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif regarding the Suthra Punjab program, the initiative allows citizens to scan codes displayed locally to access information on assigned sanitation workers and submit performance feedback.

Under this new administrative framework, authorities have been directed to address all cleanliness grievances within a matter of hours. The chief minister mandated that waste bins be installed at designated commercial and residential spots, and ordered that rural cleanliness operations be conducted at least twice per week alongside accelerated door-to-door waste collection services. Officials were further instructed to ensure equitable sanitation focus across both urban and rural jurisdictions, deploy anti-littering squads in every district, and levy financial penalties on repeat offenders caught dumping garbage improperly.

To maintain high standards, the provincial local government minister has been tasked with conducting unannounced surprise visits to monitor local sanitation arrangements, machinery functionality, and worker attendance. Daily deep-cleaning procedures have also been ordered for individual tehsils, accompanied by the deployment of modern mechanical equipment to clear roadside weeds and bushes.

Briefing participants at the meeting, officials reported that more than 93,000 sanitation beats have been established throughout Punjab. Furthermore, authorities have identified over 51,000 vacant plots, successfully clearing accumulated garbage from approximately 30,000 of them, while meeting the complete salary disbursement targets for all workers enrolled in the Suthra Punjab initiative.

stories.title: Global Oil Prices Hover Near Three-Month Low Amid Supply Surpluses
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices hovered near a three-month low on Tuesday, pressured by rising global supplies and potential market surpluses, even as geopolitical risks persisted in key shipping lanes. Brent crude futures dropped 40 cents, or 0.45%, to $88.97 a barrel by 0147 GMT, following their lowest close since October 31 on Monday. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 23 cents, or 0.29%, to $79.94 a barrel after hitting their lowest mark since August 26.

Prices received some underlying support from ongoing shipping threats in the Strait of Hormuz. According to Iran's Press TV, the Iranian Revolutionary Guards navy reported that three violating oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the strait. Additionally, the Wall Street Journal reported that US officials are investigating whether Iran may have been involved in cyberattacks targeting as many as 50 energy tankers.

Despite these security concerns, increasing output has weighed heavily on the market. Libya’s National Oil Corporation chairperson stated on Monday that the Sharara oil pipeline has reopened and flow has resumed into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya. Deutsche Bank noted that global observed liquids inventory rose by 52 million barrels in October, pointing to an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels per day. ANZ senior commodity strategist Daniel Hynes remarked that while inventories have improved, the market remains under severe strain and vulnerable to logistical constraints.

In separate domestic developments, an official communiqué confirmed that an agreement has been signed to outsource Jinnah International Airport in Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport in Lahore. The deal was finalized between the Privatization Commission and the EY Middle East Consortium to leverage private sector expertise.

stories.title: پشاور میں سی ٹی ڈی کا آپریشن، فائرنگ کے تبادلے میں پانچ دہشت گرد ہلاک
stories.summary:
پشاور کے علاقے خوڑ میرہ باچاخیل میں محکمہ انسداد دہشت گردی (سی ٹی ڈی) نے ایک خفیہ معلومات پر مبنی آپریشن کیا ہے۔ اس کارروائی کے دوران سکیورٹی فورسز اور دہشت گردوں کے درمیان تقریباً بیس سے پچیس منٹ تک فائرنگ کا تبادلہ جاری رہا، جس کے نتیجے میں پانچ دہشت گرد ہلاک ہو گئے۔

حکام کے مطابق ہلاک ہونے والے دہشت گردوں کی شناخت کا عمل فی الحال جاری ہے۔ اس فائرنگ کے تبادلے کے دوران کالعدم تنظیم کا ایک کارندہ تاج محمد اپنے دیگر ساتھیوں کے ہمراہ موقع سے فرار ہونے میں کامیاب ہو گیا۔

سی پی او کے مطابق یہ دہشت گرد سرکاری تنصیبات پر حملے کرنے اور ملک کی سلامیت کو نقصان پہنچانے کی خطرناک منصوبہ بندی کر رہے تھے۔ اس کے علاوہ وہ قانون نافذ کرنے والے اداروں کے اہلکاروں کو بھی نشانہ بنانا چاہتے تھے۔

آپریشن مکمل ہونے کے بعد سکیورٹی ٹیموں نے موقع سے بھاری مقدار میں اسلحہ برآمد کر لیا ہے۔ ہلاک شدگان کے قبضے سے تین کلاشنکوف، دو پستول اور ایک دستی بم قبضے میں لے لیا گیا ہے۔

stories.title: Australia Threatens Tech Giants with Massive Fines Over Safety Bill
stories.summary:
Australia’s centre-left Labor government has threatened major internet companies such as Google and Meta with fines reaching up to 5% of their global revenue if they fail to remove harmful content and addictive features. The new provisions were unveiled on Tuesday following an agreement with the left-leaning Greens in the Senate, significantly increasing potential penalties from a previously proposed A$109 million, given that some technology platforms generate annual revenues in the hundreds of billions of dollars.

Communications Minister Anika Wells described the legislation as urgent and seismic reform, which the government intends to pass through parliament during the week. The Digital Duty of Care law will replace existing codes of conduct across search engines, messaging apps, and AI chatbots with a unified framework requiring platforms to proactively check for and prevent harmful user experiences. Targeted harms include child sexual abuse material, non-consensual fake nudes, gender-based violence, self-harm promotion, and terrorism.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese defended the legislation in parliament, stating that the action prioritizes parents and children over foreign-owned technology companies, building on the country's social media ban for children under 16. While technology firms generally support child protection goals, many have opposed the legislation for giving government officials broad discretion in defining harmful content, arguing it could lead to heavy-handed content removal. Industry groups declined to comment on the latest draft.

In an unrelated development, an official communiqué announced that Pakistan has signed an agreement to outsource Jinnah International Airport in Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport in Lahore. The Privatization Commission and the EY Middle East Consortium signed the pact to bring private sector expertise to the management of these facilities.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Surges as KSE-100 Gains Over 1,200 Points
stories.summary:
Buying interest at the Pakistan Stock Exchange drove the benchmark KSE-100 Index up by more than 1,200 points during early trading hours on Tuesday. By 9:45 am, the index reached 178,705.34, representing an increase of 1,231.49 points or 0.69%. The positive momentum was supported by buying across major sectors, including commercial banks, automobile assemblers, fertilizers, oil and gas exploration companies, OMCs, and power generation.

Index-heavy stocks participated extensively in the upward movement, with companies such as HUBCO, ARL, MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, HBL, MEBL, MCB, and UBL trading in positive territory. This followed a mixed and range-bound session on Monday, where selective sectoral buying was offset by negative market breadth, lower ready-market turnover, and investor caution, ultimately leaving the KSE-100 up by just 91.29 points to close at 177,473.86 points.

The domestic market performance aligned with a broader global rally across Asian shares, which surged following a major Wall Street recovery. Investor sentiment globally was lifted by Jensen Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia, sparking a significant relief rally in the artificial intelligence sector. Nvidia shares jumped 31.5% on Monday, marking their largest daily percentage gain in 23 years and adding nearly $1 trillion in market value.

Reflecting the global tech rebound, regional Asian markets posted strong gains on Tuesday. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 4.6% to bounce back from an eight-month low. Japan's Nikkei added 4.5%, South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5%, and Taiwanese shares jumped 9.1%, while the Nasdaq 100 rose by more than 6%.

stories.title: Lahore High Court Rules Marriage Does Not Guarantee Origin Card
stories.summary:
The Lahore High Court has dismissed a petition filed by an American citizen of Indian origin, ruling that marriage to a Pakistani citizen does not grant an automatic right to a Pakistan Origin Card. Justice Muhammad Ajmal Zahid delivered the verdict in the case of Dr Talha Muadh Ghulam Jilani, formerly known as Dr Jaysinha Shamrao Shinde. The petitioner, who embraced Islam in 1990 and obtained US citizenship in 2007 after renouncing his Indian nationality, applied to the National Database and Registration Authority for a POC in May 2021 before his application was rejected in January 2023.

The petitioner's counsel argued that Rule 4(5) of the Nadra Rules of 2002 covers foreign spouses, asserting that Indian origin is not a legal bar and that a 2013 Interior Ministry policy cannot override statutory provisions or constitutional protections for marriage under Article 35. Conversely, a government law officer defended Nadra's decision, explaining that the 2013 policy introduced uniform mechanisms for enhanced security checks for applicants from List-B countries like India and Afghanistan due to national security concerns.

In his ruling, Justice Zahid clarified that a POC functions as a facilitation document rather than formal citizenship. He noted that while marriage establishes threshold eligibility under Rule 4(5), final issuance remains dependent on mandatory background verification and Nadra's statutory authority to decline applications in the public interest. The judge distinguished between ethnic origin and legal nationality, noting that the petitioner's renunciation certificate lacked independent verification. He affirmed that the 2013 executive policy could not alter statutory rules but served as a rational framework for security screening.

Concluding that the petitioners failed to demonstrate any jurisdictional error, arbitrariness, or mala fide exercise of power by the authorities, the court dismissed the petition. The judge emphasized that statutory relaxations for special circumstances lie within the discretionary power of the federal government and cannot be claimed as an absolute right.

stories.title: Pakistan Appoints First Astronaut for China’s Tiangong Space Station
stories.summary:
Pakistan is preparing for a major milestone in space exploration as astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has been selected to travel on China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, making him the first Pakistani visitor to the Tiangong Space Station. During a media briefing alongside fellow crew members, Ali expressed pride in carrying the hopes of 240 million citizens and praised the strong bilateral relations between Pakistan and China.

Serving as a payload specialist, Ali's core duties will involve conducting scientific research, installing experimental equipment, and taking part in joint scientific experiments between the two nations. He noted that preparation for the journey included learning the Chinese language and forging close bonds with his Chinese counterparts. Officials highlighted that the mission aims to expand Pakistan's role in international space research and enhance technological cooperation.

The Shenzhou-24 spacecraft is scheduled to lift off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre at 8:18 a.m. China Standard Time. This deployment marks an important step in expanding international cooperation at the Chinese space station.

Separately, an official communiqué confirmed that an agreement has been signed to outsource Jinnah International Airport in Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport in Lahore. The Privatization Commission and the EY Middle East Consortium finalized the deal to bring private sector expertise to the management of both facilities.

stories.title: Kuwait Introduces Smart Licensing System with Integrated QR Codes
stories.summary:
Kuwait's Ministry of Commerce and Industry is implementing a unified smart licensing framework to streamline business procedures across the nation. The initiative introduces integrated QR codes on commercial licences to allow electronic verification, effectively removing the requirement for establishments such as shops, cafés, and restaurants to exhibit multiple paper documents issued by various government bodies. This shift supports the country's broader digital transformation goals.

Acting Undersecretary Marwa Al-Juaidan stated that the system seeks to refine the business environment, simplify administrative steps, and boost inter-agency coordination. She highlighted that the embedded QR code will act as the main tool for checking licence credentials, which is expected to raise regulatory efficiency, speed up inspections, and ease government services.

The smart licensing project, launched in 2025, involves nine entities including the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Kuwait Municipality, Kuwait Fire Force, and several authorities focused on manpower, food, information, industry, capital markets, and civil information. A circular is being prepared to mandate reliance on the barcode system and identify technical bottlenecks.

Concurrently, the Public Authority for Manpower noted that specific employment rules must still be physically shown under Kuwait's Labour Law No. 6 of 2010. Spokesperson Mohammad Al-Muzaini pointed out that articles 35 and 82 mandate the display of disciplinary regulations and notices concerning working hours and holidays. While Ministerial Decision No. 15 of 2025 permits digital submissions, the physical documents remain legally required at workplaces.

The manpower authority is pursuing legal amendments to align with technological advances and expand electronic administration. These changes aim to ease digital access to workplace rules, lower burdens on employers, and help inspectors verify compliance while safeguarding labour rights and employer obligations.

stories.title: پاکستان میں نئے صوبوں کے قیام اور ریفرنڈم کے طریقہ کار پر بحث
stories.summary:
پاکستان میں نئے صوبوں کے قیام کے معاملے پر سیاسی اور آئینی حلقوں میں بحث شدت اختیار کر گئی ہے۔ وفاقی حکومت نے ریفرنڈم کے ذریعے نئے صوبے بنانے کا عزم ظاہر کیا ہے، جبکہ اپوزیشن جماعتیں اور آئینی ماہرین اس کے طریقہ کار پر سوالات اٹھا رہے ہیں۔

وزیر داخلہ محسن نقوی نے بارہ نومبر کو اسلام آباد میں دعویٰ کیا تھا کہ عوامی جائزوں کے مطابق اکثریت نئے صوبوں کے حق میں ہے، اس لیے ریفرنڈم ہونا چاہیے۔ دوسری جانب پیپلز پارٹی اور سندھ کی قوم پرست جماعتیں سندھ کی تقسیم کی سخت مخالفت کر رہی ہیں اور اس سلسلے میں سندھ اسمبلی میں ایک قرارداد بھی منظور کی جا چکی ہے۔

آئینی ماہرین کے مطابق آئین کے آرٹیکل اڑتالیس کی شق چھ کے تحت وزیراعظم کابینہ کے مشورہ سے پارلیمان کے مشترکہ اجلاس میں ریفرنڈم کا معاملہ رکھ سکتے ہیں۔ سابق اٹارنی جنرل بیرسٹر اشتر اوصاف کا کہنا ہے کہ ریفرنڈم محض عوامی رائے ہے اور اس کی کوئی قانونی بائنڈنگ اتھارٹی نہیں ہوتی۔

آئین کے آرٹیکل دو سو انتالیس کی شق چار کے تحت کسی بھی صوبے کی تقسیم کے لیے متعلقہ صوبائی اسمبلی کی دو تہائی اکثریت کی منظوری لازمی ہے۔ ماہرین کے مابین اس بات پر اختلاف ہے کہ آیا عوامی ریفرنڈم کے بعد صوبائی اسمبلی کا ویٹو کا اختیار ختم ہو جاتا ہے یا برقرار رہتا ہے۔

stories.title: Zeeshan Ali to Become First Pakistani Astronaut Aboard China's Mission
stories.summary:
Zeeshan Ali has been selected as a crew member for China's Shenzhou-24 space mission, slated for launch on November 25. The China Manned Space Agency announced that Ali will make history as the first Pakistani to undertake a space mission and the first foreign national to board Beijing's Tiangong space station, serving as a payload specialist during the flight.

The spacecraft is scheduled to lift off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, with Ali spending roughly a week in orbit. He will work alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, participating in an estimated 90 experiments, routine station maintenance, and an orbital crew rotation with the Shenzhou-23 team before returning on the latter spacecraft.

At a press briefing in Jiayuguan, Ali expressed gratitude to the Chinese government and reflected on his comprehensive training at the Astronaut Centre of China. He emphasized that the milestone represents the shared dreams of 250 million Pakistanis and underscores the enduring diplomatic and space cooperation ties between Pakistan and China, coinciding with upcoming anniversary milestones.

Punjab Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar congratulated Ali, describing the joint endeavor as a testament to the iron brotherhood between the two nations. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif previously met with Ali and fellow astronaut candidate Khurram Daud in April, praising their selection as a source of national pride.

The mission reflects Beijing's expanding partnerships in space exploration following restrictions on its participation in the International Space Station since 2011. Following a cooperation agreement signed between Suparco and the CMSA in February 2025, the flight marks a significant step in bilateral scientific collaboration and peaceful space utilization.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia Faces Criticism Over Fossil Fuel Stance at COP31 Talks
stories.summary:
The 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference in Antalya concluded in record overtime without a political agreement, driven largely by sharp divisions over fossil fuels. Negotiators from various global regions reported that Saudi Arabia exerted disproportionate influence during the summit, successfully resisting any text that called for reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

Delegates from the European Union, small island states, and other vulnerable nations argued that a final deal omitted crucial references to coal, oil, and gas. Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU, accused oil states of hijacking the conference. Conversely, the Turkish COP presidency maintained that no country received preferential treatment, while representatives for Saudi Arabia and Australia did not immediately comment.

Several delegates noted that Riyadh's position was bolstered by the absence of active US engagement and a lack of US-China coordination seen in past summits. Singapore Environment Minister Grace Fu remarked that the boundaries of discussion became less clear. Saudi officials maintained a firm stance throughout the second week, advocating instead for carbon capture technologies.

As discussions stalled, the EU adopted a rigid stance for a comprehensive deal or none at all. Germany subsequently gathered vulnerable nations, African countries, and developed economies into the High Ambition Coalition to submit an alternate proposal backed by approximately 130 countries, urging a transition away from fossil fuels while rejecting carbon capture references.

stories.title: Kuwait Ministry Warns Chalet Beneficiaries Against Housing Residency Violators
stories.summary:
Kuwait's Ministry of Finance has issued a formal warning to beneficiaries of state-owned chalets, prohibiting them from employing or accommodating individuals who breach the nation's residency and labour laws. The restriction applies uniformly regardless of the specific capacity, role, or title of the workers involved.

To enforce these rules, the ministry announced upcoming field inspection campaigns through the General Department of State Property Affairs. Inspection teams will visit state-owned chalet facilities alongside relevant authorities to monitor adherence, identify infractions, and document any illegal employment or housing arrangements for subsequent legal action.

The General Department of State Property Affairs emphasized its mandate to protect public assets and ensure state properties are utilized strictly for their intended purposes and legal guidelines. State-allocated private properties must not be exploited to harbour individuals who contravene official labour and residency regulations.

The ministry has called upon all chalet beneficiaries to verify the legal status of any workers present on their premises and to extend full cooperation to visiting inspectors. Officials reiterated that enforcement and monitoring operations will persist to safeguard public property and maintain strict adherence to Kuwaiti legislation.

stories.title: Australia Proposes Massive Fines for Tech Giants Under New Safety Bill
stories.summary:
Australia is advancing a new legislative measure known as the Digital Duty of Care law, which targets major internet corporations such as Google and Meta. Announced in Sydney, the proposed framework threatens non-compliant technology firms with financial penalties reaching up to five percent of their global revenue if they fail to eliminate harmful digital content and addictive features. This penalty structure represents a substantial increase from a previously considered fine of A$109 million, equivalent to $72.2 million, which had faced widespread criticism.

The initiative follows an agreement struck between the centre-left Labor government and the left-leaning Greens within the Senate, placing the bill on a clear path toward parliamentary approval. Communications Minister Anika Wells described the legislation as a vital and urgent reform destined for passage during the parliamentary session. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese emphasized that the initiative positions the nation alongside families and children rather than foreign-owned technology enterprises, building upon the country's prior implementation of a world-first social media ban for individuals under the age of sixteen.

Under the new legal framework, a fragmented collection of enforceable codes governing various online industries—ranging from messaging applications and search engines to artificial intelligence chatbots—will be superseded by a unified mandate requiring companies to proactively intercept harmful user experiences. Specific categories of targeted abuse comprise material depicting child sexual abuse, non-consensual deepfake nude imagery, gender-based violence, the promotion of self-harm, and terrorism.

Despite the government's stated objectives of enhancing child safety, technology corporations and industry advocates have voiced objections. Most opponents argue that the legislation grants excessive discretionary authority to government officials in determining what constitutes harmful material. Industry representatives previously cautioned that such ambiguity might incentivize platforms to adopt overly aggressive content-removal practices to evade severe financial punishment.

stories.title: پنجاب میں بلدیاتی انتخابات کے انعقاد اور تیاریاں مکمل ہیں: عظمیٰ بخاری
stories.summary:
پنجاب کی وزیر اطلاعات عظمیٰ بخاری نے کہا ہے کہ صوبے میں بلدیاتی انتخابات کرانے کے لیے تمام انتظامات مکمل ہیں اور حکومت بھرپور طریقے سے تیار ہے۔ انہوں نے واضح کیا کہ جیسے ہی الیکشن کمیشن کی جانب سے بلدیاتی انتخاب کا باقاعدہ شیڈول جاری کیا جائے گا، اس پر عمل درآمد کیا جائے گا۔

اپنے ایک بیان میں انہوں نے مزید کہا کہ اس وقت ان کی جماعت کے ارکان اور رہنما متعلقہ حلقوں میں جا کر بلدیاتی انتخابات کے لیے موزوں امیدواروں کی تلاش کا عمل جاری رکھے ہوئے ہیں۔ ماضی کے حوالے سے بات کرتے ہوئے ان کا کہنا تھا کہ پنجاب میں جتنے بھی ماضی میں انتخابات ہوئے ہیں وہ ن لیگ کے دور میں ہی منعقد کیے گئے ہیں۔

وزیر اطلاعات نے اس بات پر بھی زور دیا کہ موجودہ وزیراعظم شہباز شریف تمام اتحادی جماعتوں کو ساتھ لے کر چل رہے ہیں اور ملک کے اہم قومی ایشوز کو کسی بھی صورت متنازع نہیں بننے دینا چاہیے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ اتحادی حکومت کو بخوبی علم ہے کہ اہم معاملات پر کس طرح سے لینی ہے۔

اس کے علاوہ پنجاب میں سرکاری امور اور سیاسی صورتحال پر بات کرتے ہوئے انہوں نے وفاقی اور صوبائی تعاون کو سراہا۔ عظمیٰ بخاری نے یہ بھی بتایا کہ لاہور ہائیکورٹ میں ان کے ویڈیو لنک بیان پر جرح کے لیے باقاعدہ ایک درخواست دائر کر دی گئی ہے۔

stories.title: دھند اور فنی خرابی کے باعث سیالکوٹ اور اسلام آباد کی پروازیں متاثر
stories.summary:
شدید دھند اور ناگزیر فنی خرابیوں کے باعث ملک کے اہم ہوائی اڈوں پر فضائی آپریشن متاثر ہوا ہے، جس کے نتیجے میں سیالکوٹ اور اسلام آباد کی دو پروازوں کی متبادل لینڈنگ کرائی گئی ہے۔ فلائٹ شیڈول کے مطابق جدہ سے اسلام آباد آنے والی پرواز ایس وی 726 میں فنی خرابی پیدا ہو گئی تھی۔

فنی خرابی کے باعث اس پرواز کو شیڈول کے برعکس دمام کے ایئرپورٹ پر اتارنا پڑا، جہاں طیارہ تبدیل کیا گیا اور پھر یہ پرواز چھ گھنٹے کی طویل تاخیر کے بعد اسلام آباد پہنچی۔ اسی طرح مسقط سے سیالکوٹ آنے والی پرواز او وی 505 کو بھی خراب موسم اور شدید دھند کی وجہ سے پہلے اسلام آباد میں اتارا گیا۔

موسم کی صورتحال بہتر ہونے کے بعد مسقط سے آنے والی اس پرواز کو بعد میں اسلام آباد سے سیالکوٹ روانہ کیا گیا۔ مسقط کے لیے واپسی کی پرواز او وی 506 کی روانگی میں بھی پانچ گھنٹے کی تاخیر ریکارڈ کی گئی ہے۔

فلائٹ شیڈول کے مطابق ملتان سے جدہ جانے والی پروازیں پی کے 739 اور 840 چودہ گھنٹے جبکہ لاہور سے جدہ اور ریاض جانے والی پروازیں آٹھ سے بارہ گھنٹے تک کی تاخیر کا شکار ہوئی ہیں، جس سے مسافروں کو مشکلات کا سامنا کرنا پڑا۔

stories.title: South Korea Implements Strict Anti-Cheating Measures Following Tech Scandal
stories.summary:
South Korea has introduced stringent regulations designed to eliminate exam cheating in middle and high schools, following a prominent national controversy involving technology-assisted fraud. Acting Education Minister Choi Eun-ok announced the updated guidelines during a cabinet meeting on Tuesday. Under the revised framework, students caught possessing or utilizing a smart device during a regular school examination will receive a grade of zero across every single subject tested on that day.

The policy response was precipitated by a high-profile scandal in which the top scorer of a national tax-accountant examination confessed to employing a miniature camera, a smartphone, and artificial intelligence to cheat. Because internal assessments directly influence university admissions, the government aims to close loopholes where penalties were previously restricted to invalidating only the specific exam during which an infraction occurred. Alongside receiving failing marks for the entire day, offending students face severe disciplinary repercussions, including potential expulsion.

To enforce the mandate, educational institutions will implement rigorous preventative procedures on test days. Schools are required to collect cellular telephones and electronic devices prior to testing, store student bags away from examination rooms, disable campus wireless internet services, and actively monitor local wireless signals for suspicious data transmissions. Furthermore, students may be subjected to metal-detector screenings both before entering examination rooms and upon returning from restroom breaks. The Ministry of Education also intends to pursue legal amendments to broaden sanctions, prolong test-taking bans, and establish a firm statutory foundation for institutional inspections.

President Lee Jae Myung condemned academic cheating as a grave offense capable of destabilizing societal foundations, directing authorities to enforce rigorous countermeasures across school assessments, professional qualifications, and public-sector recruitment examinations. This policy push follows the resignation of former Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin, which President Lee accepted on Sunday amid administrative confusion surrounding last-minute anti-cheating protocols for a national test administered the previous week. Concurrently, the ministry has initiated criminal complaints regarding five separate instances where students were discovered with illicit technology, including smart glasses, miniature cameras, wireless earphones, and smartphones.

stories.title: Pakistan Stock Exchange Closes Flat Amid Cautious Investor Sentiment
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a volatile trading session on Monday, characterized by investor caution stemming from escalating tensions in the Middle East and domestic political friction surrounding a proposed administrative referendum to create new provinces. Despite falling crude oil prices, market participants remained vigilant as the benchmark KSE-100 index fluctuated in both directions before closing with marginal gains, aided by late buying support at lower valuation levels.

According to Topline Securities Ltd, the index initially built upon its early recovery before surrendering the majority of its intraday advances. The benchmark reached an intraday peak of 178,746.45 points and dipped to a low of 177,357.46 points, ultimately settling at 177,473.86 points. This final figure represented a minor increase of 91.29 points, or 0.05 percent, resulting in a virtually flat daily performance as profit-taking eroded earlier market gains. Key corporate entities including Engro Holdings, Hub Power, Mari Energies, Pakistan Services, and The Searle served as the primary positive drivers, collectively contributing approximately 411 points to the index.

Conversely, downward pressure from Engro Fertilisers, Oil and Gas Development Company, and Systems Ltd erased roughly 135 points, mitigating the positive momentum. Trading participation deteriorated as total market volume contracted by 11.15 percent to settle at 551.5 million shares, while overall turnover edged down by 0.42 percent to Rs22.5 billion. WorldCall Telecom led the volume rankings with 88.79 million shares traded. In corporate developments, Nishat Chunian Ltd formally notified the stock exchange of its intention to repurchase 50.4 million shares, representing 21 percent of its total issued and paid-up capital, across a period extending from November 30 to May 19, 2027.

External geopolitical factors also weighed on the broader financial outlook. United States President Donald Trump signaled that Washington might restart military operations against Iran next year if diplomatic negotiations fail to produce a resolution, attributing Tehran's assertive posture to his own political party's recent electoral defeat. Financial analysts anticipate that the local market will continue trading sideways, identifying support levels between 175,000 and 176,000 points, with an upside target of 182,500 points once the current consolidation phase concludes.

stories.title: Surge in Used Phone Imports Threatens Local Pakistani Manufacturing Industry
stories.summary:
Imports of used smartphones into Pakistan experienced a dramatic escalation, climbing from 1,434 units in July to 98,383 units in October. This influx coincided with a narrowing tariff gap between locally manufactured devices and imported alternatives. Overall smartphone arrivals reached 150,133 units in October—including 51,750 new devices valued at $71.7 million—compared with 18,431 smartphones valued at $17.8 million in July. Completely built-up units have rapidly captured 41.8 percent of the domestic smartphone market over the course of several months.

In response to these developments, the Pakistan Mobile Phone Manufacturers Association submitted a formal letter to the Ministry of Industries and Production and the Federal Board of Revenue, highlighting the alarming rise in used phone imports. Association representatives are scheduled to meet with government officials in Islamabad to address the crisis. Industry leaders warn that the trend is severely undermining local assembly operations, noting that domestic production dropped from 906,711 units in July to 752,870 units in October.

PMPMA Chairman Abdul Rehman explained that the surge in imports is propelled by two primary catalysts: compressed import duty differentials that encourage informal commercial networks known as the 'khepia' business, and downward adjustments in FBR tax valuations. The tariff disparity between fully assembled smartphones and knocked-down kits intended for domestic production has shrunk to approximately 11 percent for a $100 device and 14 percent for a $200 device. Because this $100 to $200 tier represents the highest-selling market segment, the narrow margin has effectively vanished due to practices such as under-invoicing, marginalizing regulated local producers.

Mr Rehman further noted that reduced FBR valuations under the Device Identification, Registration and Blocking System have enabled inexpensive imported phones to easily gain registration through the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority. The manufacturing sector has battled what it terms reverse cascading taxation for three years, which has prevented the localization of core components such as chargers, batteries, cables, and motherboard assemblies. While a charger can currently be imported duty-free inside a knocked-down kit, importing its raw materials and subcomponents incurs a cumulative duty of nearly 20 percent.

stories.title: US President Trump to Meet NATO Chief Mark Rutte in Florida
stories.summary:
United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet North Atlantic Treaty Organization chief Mark Rutte late Wednesday afternoon in Palm Beach, Florida. The White House announced the upcoming meeting on Monday, noting that it follows Trump's recent discussions in Asia with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

The upcoming talks arrive amid ongoing tensions within the Western military alliance. Trump has frequently taken aim at democratic allies over trade tariffs, defense spending, and what he characterizes as insufficient backing for Washington during the US-Israeli war in Iran. Furthermore, Trump's recent summit interactions, where he labeled both Putin and Xi as his friends, drew a sharp backlash from Democratic opponents domestically and various European allies.

Meanwhile, European leaders have actively sought inclusion in US-supported negotiations aimed at settling the ongoing war in Ukraine. During recent outreach to allies, US special envoy and presidential son-in-law Jared Kushner indicated that Moscow had grown comfortable with potential security guarantees for Ukraine modeled after the alliance's Article 5 mutual defense agreement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who has faced criticism from Trump, has repeatedly insisted that Europe must take part in any formal peace talks.

Despite the friction, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has consistently worked to keep Trump aligned and calm tensions within the alliance, previously describing interactions between major nuclear powers as routine. The Florida meeting serves as an opportunity for both leaders to address alliance concerns and Europe's involvement in future diplomatic resolutions regarding Ukraine.

stories.title: Pakistan Food Exports Rise as Wheat Imports Resume in October
stories.summary:
Pakistan initiated its sugar export season for the current fiscal year by shipping 10,346 tonnes abroad in October, according to official figures compiled by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. Concurrently, wheat imports resumed during the month, with 51,000 tonnes brought into the country to address domestic supply deficits and stabilize rising food costs. The October sugar shipment volume remained far below previous government-approved quotas, which included 108,000 tonnes in August and 200,000 tonnes in mid-September, with no exports recorded during those prior two months. The Economic Coordination Committee of the Cabinet subsequently cleared an additional export quota of 416,000 tonnes.

Total food exports climbed by 22.49 percent to reach $1.885 billion between July and October of fiscal year 2027, up from $1.538 billion during the same period the previous year. October sugar exports alone generated $4.936 million. Other agricultural sectors saw mixed results during the four-month period; meat exports grew by 19 percent, fish and fish products rose by 29.83 percent, and spice exports expanded by 23.98 percent. Conversely, vegetable and fruit exports experienced declines of 18.64 percent and 27.43 percent, respectively. Traditional export markets include Afghanistan, China, and Iran, though no fruit or vegetable shipments to Afghanistan have been documented since October 2025.

On the import side, palm oil constituted the largest share of incoming food products, followed by pulses, tea, and soybean oil. Palm oil import values grew modestly by 1.44 percent despite a 9.60 percent drop in total import volumes. Conversely, pulse imports decreased by 10.02 percent, and soybean oil values dropped sharply by 90.35 percent compared to the prior year. Meanwhile, import bills for milk products, dry fruits, tea, and other food commodities registered increases.

Overall, Pakistan's total import bill experienced a modest 2.76 percent growth, reaching $3.160 billion for the first four months of fiscal year 2027, compared to $3.075 billion in the corresponding timeframe last year. The shifting trade figures highlight ongoing adjustments in the country's agricultural economy as officials balance domestic supply shortages against international market demands.

stories.title: Cyber Crime Agency Arrests Four in Online Romance Fraud Case
stories.summary:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency arrested four suspects in connection with an online romance scam and financial fraud. Operating under the supervision of Additional Director Atif Ameer, law enforcement teams carried out two separate raids in Rahim Yar Khan and Lodhran to apprehend the individuals involved in the criminal ring.

According to preliminary findings from the investigation, the suspects used popular digital platforms including TikTok and WhatsApp to cultivate a close emotional relationship with a female victim. They subsequently convinced her that a diamond ring valued at 10,000 United States dollars was being dispatched to her from the United Kingdom. Posing as government officials, the perpetrators then persuaded the victim to deposit funds into various designated bank accounts. Through this elaborate deception, the group allegedly defrauded the woman of approximately 5.809 million Pakistani rupees.

During the course of the raids, authorities recovered three mobile phones and one vehicle. Investigators also secured critical digital evidence, which included forged payment receipts and suspicious chat logs retrieved from WhatsApp. Law enforcement officials stated that further inquiries are currently underway to uncover additional details and trace the full scope of the operation.

In a separate case handled by the agency, the NCCIA in Islamabad successfully recovered 2.94 million rupees and returned the funds to a female complainant who had suffered a 9.5 million rupee loss in a separate online financial fraud incident. That inquiry was conducted under the oversight of Inspector Waqar Masih Ghouri, with investigations continuing to track down the remaining missing funds and identify all responsible parties.

stories.title: FoodAg Pakistan Exhibition Highlights Growth in Agricultural Export Sector
stories.summary:
Commerce Minister Jam Kamal announced a notable increase in international attendance at the fourth International Food and Agro Exhibition, known as FoodAg Pakistan, despite regional security concerns and shipping disruptions near the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking to the media after inaugurating the four-day event at the Karachi Expo Centre on Monday, the minister emphasized that the exhibition has successfully expanded its reach over the past four years, offering local agricultural producers, business owners, and exporters vital networking avenues with global buyers and investors.

Organized by the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan, the event runs from November 23 to 26 and brings together 400 domestic exhibitors alongside 820 international delegates representing 72 countries. Participating sectors span a wide variety of goods, including rice, fruits, vegetables, meat, poultry, dairy, fisheries, seafood, processed snacks, spices, honey, and food-related services. The minister noted that business-to-business meetings remain crucial for direct engagement, even as rising freight expenses and crude oil prices present ongoing hurdles for international commerce.

During his address, Kamal highlighted positive economic indicators, pointing out that Pakistan's services exports recently surpassed the one billion dollar milestone, while agriculture, information technology, and textiles continued to drive export performance despite global uncertainty. Addressing regional trade, he mentioned that commerce with Afghanistan has faced challenges due to national security necessities, with Islamabad urging Afghan authorities to crack down on groups using their territory against Pakistan. Furthermore, he noted ongoing discussions with Chinese enterprises regarding product sales, observing that annual imports from China traditionally range between $17 billion and $18 billion compared to roughly $3 billion in exports.

The inaugural gala dinner for the exhibition was hosted at the Governor House in Karachi on November 23, featuring addresses from officials such as Sindh Governor Nehal Hashmi. The opening ceremony drew a diverse gathering of dignitaries, foreign delegates, regulatory representatives, and prominent members of the domestic business community.

stories.title: Nvidia Shares Surge Following Jensen Huang's Return as CEO
stories.summary:
Shares in artificial intelligence chip giant Nvidia jumped 30 percent on Monday after the unexpected reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang. Huang's return helped spark a broad market recovery following a tech-led rout last week that saw major indices dive between seven and 10 percent. Wealth Club chief investment strategist Susannah Streeter noted that while Huang is an AI comeback kid, volatility persists as the company remains under scrutiny from investigators including the FBI and Capitol Hill over the spy scandal that preceded his initial resignation.

US President Donald Trump publicly backed the decision, stating on social media that the government has no reason to believe Huang's return poses any national security risk. The announcement propelled the tech-heavy Nasdaq up by seven percent, the Dow by 2.6 percent, and the S&P 500 by five percent within two hours of the session. European markets also experienced gains, with Frankfurt rising 2.2 percent and London and Paris seeing increases of about 1.5 percent.

Conversely, Asian markets suffered heavy tech sell-offs, with South Korea's Seoul sliding over three percent. Semiconductor suppliers SK Hynix and Samsung saw continued weakness, indicating ongoing investor caution. Authorities globally have introduced measures to counter negative impacts, such as Taiwan tightening rules on shorting stocks, China easing borrowing to purchase shares, and South Korea considering a stabilisation fund not utilized since the global financial crisis.

In commodities, US West Texas Intermediate oil fell four percent to drop below $80 for the first time since August due to expectations of an oversupplied market, despite ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. Brent North Sea crude similarly slipped four percent to $88.93 a barrel. Meanwhile, Kuwait's Ministry of Commerce and Industry announced steps to streamline commercial licensing through a unified smart system utilizing integrated QR codes to eliminate paper displays.

stories.title: Pakistani Minister Attends SCO Forum in India Amid Frozen Ties
stories.summary:
Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik recently traveled to New Delhi to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. Bilateral engagement between Pakistan and India remains near zero primarily due to New Delhi's rigidity, and last year's armed conflict created a toxic regional atmosphere. Although the multilateral meeting carried no expectations of a bilateral breakthrough, the visit itself is seen as a welcome development capable of helping lower regional temperatures and confrontational rhetoric.

During the event, Mr. Malik emphasized the threat of climate change to the entire region and highlighted the shared civilisational bonds connecting South Asia and Eurasia. He also addressed pointed inquiries from the Indian media regarding terrorism and the Indus Waters Treaty by clarifying that he was present for an SCO event and that specific bilateral grievances could be discussed when formally invited by India, noting Pakistan holds its own concerns.

Editorial commentary stresses that structured dialogue remains the only viable path to peace and satisfactory resolution of concerns in South Asia. While Pakistan has defended itself against past aggression and stands ready to respond to future threats, the region's people deserve a peaceful future rather than eternal conflict. Observers note that whenever India is prepared to engage in respectful and frank dialogue, Pakistan will respond accordingly.

stories.title: Ousted Leader Sheikh Hasina Plans December Return to Bangladesh
stories.summary:
Ousted former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina intends to return to her home country on December 16, marking the anniversary of the 1971 liberation war's end, according to her spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali. This marks the first time Hasina has specified a return date after more than two years of exile in India. Her plans could escalate political and legal tensions in Bangladesh, where her party is banned and unrest has increased following her recent efforts to secure a new passport and travel documents.

Hasina fled to Delhi on August 5, 2024, aboard a Bangladeshi aircraft following a deadly student-led uprising that resulted in up to 1,400 deaths according to United Nations figures. Her spokesperson argued that because she was exiled contrary to the constitution, the government is responsible for arranging her return flight on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines for Victory Day. A Bangladeshi government spokesperson did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the transport request.

A Bangladeshi minister stated that Hasina faces a death sentence and would be arrested and imprisoned immediately upon her return, adding that no official discussions have occurred with India regarding an aircraft to bring her back. In November of last year, a Bangladeshi war crimes court sentenced her to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown during the uprising, charges which she has consistently denied from exile.

stories.title: Anthropic Options Launch with Strong Volume but Trail SpaceX Record
stories.summary:
Anthropic experienced a robust market debut for its newly listed options on Monday, recording 500,000 contracts exchanged by 3 p.m. EST. This heavy trading activity placed the artificial intelligence developer among the 20 most actively traded names in the options market for the day, according to analytics provider Mercury Alerts. Options provide market participants with a cost-efficient method to speculate on price direction or hedge against financial risk.

Despite the brisk start, the initial volume fell significantly short of the 1.8 million contracts traded during the launch of SpaceX options earlier in the year. Market participants noted that trading was notably balanced, with call and put options trading in a one-to-one ratio and buyers nearly matching sellers without a clear directional bias. Analysts attributed the tamer speculation partly to the absence of the enthusiasm typically driven by Elon Musk's involvement in companies like SpaceX.

Broader market movements and external news also impacted trading interest in Anthropic derivatives. Traders observed that a wider market rally lifting AI-related stocks, alongside attention drawn to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement, likely diverted trading focus. Furthermore, the current lack of weekly contracts, which are traditionally popular among retail investors, may have constrained overall volumes.

Prices in the options market indicate that investors anticipate notable share price movement for Anthropic going forward. According to analytics data, the derivatives are pricing in daily swings of approximately 6%. Meanwhile, Anthropic shares experienced a decline of 3.6%, closing at $85.68.

stories.title: US Senate Panel Investigates JD Vance Over Venezuelan Oil Contract
stories.summary:
A United States Senate committee has launched an inquiry into Vice President JD Vance regarding his alleged involvement in awarding a lucrative Venezuelan oil marketing contract to commodities firm Vitol. Senator Maggie Hassan, a New Hampshire Democrat who is set to lead the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee in January, sent a letter to Vance requesting documents and communications by December 14 concerning the deal.

The investigation stems from a meeting between Vance and Vitol gasoline trader John Addison that took place in December 2025 at Montana's Yellowstone Club. According to a source familiar with the matter, Vance inquired about how rapidly Venezuelan crude could be marketed if the United States assumed control of the country's oil supplies, and Addison asserted that Vitol was well-prepared for the task. Both Vance and Addison have denied that the meeting occurred, although flight records reportedly place their respective aircraft at the same airport on that day.

The political fallout connects to events surrounding the ouster of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro following a US operation in January. Addison confirmed that US Energy Secretary Chris Wright contacted him on January 5 to offer Vitol the opportunity to sell Venezuelan oil to finance the political transition. Within days, Vitol and rival firm Trafigura secured special licenses, subsequently generating hundreds of millions of dollars. The State Department reported that the US handled over $12 billion in Venezuelan oil revenue during the first nine months of the year.

Financial disclosures indicate a history of political donations linking Addison to Vance and President Donald Trump. Federal Election Commission records show Addison contributed $300,000 in 2022 to a political action committee supporting Vance's Senate campaign. Additionally, Addison and his wife contributed $7 million in 2024 to support Trump's successful return to the White House.

stories.title: Ousted Leader Sheikh Hasina Plans Return to Bangladesh on December 16
stories.summary:
Ousted former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina intends to return from her exile in India on December 16, marking her first specific timeline for coming back since fleeing the country. Her spokesperson announced the plan, calling upon the Bangladeshi government to provide state air transport via the national carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines, for her journey from Delhi to Dhaka on Victory Day.

Hasina left Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a massive student-led uprising that the United Nations estimates resulted in approximately 1,400 deaths. Her passport and other documents were subsequently cancelled. Earlier this month, she sought new travel paperwork and urged authorities to facilitate her return, arguing that her exile violated the Constitution and that the state bears the responsibility for her repatriation.

The proposed return threatens to heighten political and legal friction in Bangladesh, where Hasina's political party remains banned and unrest has persisted. A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters that Hasina would face immediate arrest and imprisonment upon arrival, noting that no formal discussions had taken place with Indian authorities regarding an official flight to bring her back.

In November of last year, a Bangladeshi war crimes court sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for her role in ordering the deadly crackdown during the uprising that ousted her. Hasina has consistently denied all charges against her while remaining in exile in India, setting the stage for potential confrontation should her return proceed.

stories.title: Crude prices hover near three-month low amidst rising supplies
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices hovered near a three-month low on Tuesday, pressured by increasing global supplies and a potential market surplus, even as maritime shipping risks persisted through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures fell 40 cents to $88.97 a barrel following their lowest close since October 31, while US West Texas Intermediate dropped 23 cents to $79.94 a barrel.

The downward price movement was driven by recovering production and inventory growth. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline reopened, directing flows to storage tanks in Zawiya, according to the chairperson of the National Oil Corporation. Furthermore, Deutsche Bank noted that global observed liquids inventory rose by 52 million barrels in October, indicating a daily oversupply of 1.7 million barrels.

Despite the oversupply trend, geopolitical tensions provided a floor for prices. Iran's Press TV reported that three oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while US officials investigated potential Iranian cyberattacks targeting nearly 50 energy tankers.

Analysts noted that the oil market remains fragile despite improving inventories. Daniel Hynes, a senior commodity strategist at ANZ, stated that the system is shifting from acute scarcity to persistent vulnerability. A preliminary Reuters poll also suggested that US crude and product inventories likely increased over the previous week.

stories.title: Pakistan petroleum dealers threaten strike over daily pricing policy
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) issued a 15-day ultimatum on Monday warning that dealers will shut down petrol pumps across the country unless the government abandons its daily fuel pricing mechanism. Speaking at a press conference at the Karachi Press Club, PPDA Chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh and other association leaders argued that daily price adjustments rapidly deplete working capital, which could lead to pumps running dry and causing law and order issues.

The dealers demanded an immediate increase in their profit margins to 8 percent of the retail price. They also claimed that local refineries have reduced supplies of petrol and diesel, with one refinery completely halting diesel deliveries. The PPDA stated that its members collectively deposit Rs5.74 billion into the national exchequer daily.

This confrontation follows months of friction between fuel retailers and the government over pricing policies. The daily pricing system was introduced in July by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik to manage international market volatility. Previous strike threats in March, July, and August were averted after government interventions, which included a 15.5 percent increase in dealers' margins on September 1, raising the rate by Rs1.34 to Rs9.98 per litre.

Fuel prices have recently decreased, with petrol dropping from Rs369.60 per litre on November 4 to Rs322. However, dealers asserted that the daily adjustments remain financially unsustainable. They urged authorities to implement a 30-day pricing mechanism similar to those enjoyed by refineries and oil marketing companies, and insisted that no fuel-related policies should be enacted without consulting them.

stories.title: US dollar nears 20-month high as Nvidia CEO return boosts rates
stories.summary:
The US dollar traded near a 20-month high on Tuesday as Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO of Nvidia revived enthusiasm for artificial intelligence investments. The equity rally renewed expectations that economic resilience will grant the Federal Reserve greater latitude to pursue additional interest rate hikes.

The surging dollar impacted major global currencies significantly. The euro languished near an 18-month low at $1.0907 following an overnight decline of 0.6 percent, while sterling remained depressed near a one-year low at $1.3037. The dollar index firmed at 104.32, having touched 104.53 in the previous session. Nvidia reinstated Huang under pressure from US President Donald Trump, adding approximately $950 billion to its market capitalization overnight.

Market expectations for monetary policy shifted sharply following the equity rebound. According to the CME FedWatch tool, traders fully priced in a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike for the following month, with a small probability introduced for an outsized 50-basis-point increase. This reversed cautious sentiment from the previous week, when a technology and chip stock selloff had led investors to scale back tightening bets.

Other regional currencies also experienced pressure. The Japanese yen eased to 159.06 per dollar, while the Australian dollar stayed pinned near an 11-month low at $0.6627. J.P. Morgan analysts reported that short positions and bearish options positioning against the Australian dollar reached extreme levels as domestic markets priced in future rate cuts.

stories.title: Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Threaten Strike Over Daily Fuel Pricing
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association warned on Monday that petrol pumps will close unless the government transitions fuel pricing from a daily mechanism to a 30-day fixed model, giving authorities a 15-day window to resolve the issue. At a press conference in Karachi, association leaders stated that daily price fluctuations are rapidly depleting pump owners' working capital, risking dry pumps and potential law and order situations. They also reiterated demands for an immediate dealer margin increase of eight percent of the retail price and claimed that local refineries have reduced or entirely halted supplies of petrol and diesel.

Association Chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh noted that while previous strike threats were withdrawn following government intervention and minor margin adjustments—such as a 15.5 percent margin increase approved by the ECC in September—core issues like the daily pricing regime introduced in July remain unaddressed. Despite falling retail prices, with petrol dropping from Rs369.60 on November 4 to Rs322, dealers argue that continuous adjustments create severe financial hardship. The association insists that future petroleum policies must involve direct consultation with dealers rather than arbitrary implementation.

stories.title: Asian Markets Rally as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Returns
stories.summary:
Asian stock markets experienced a substantial rally on Tuesday, driven by Wall Street's strong performance following Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. This leadership comeback triggered a relief rally that lifted battered artificial intelligence stocks globally, helping MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climb 4.6% from an eight-month low for its biggest single-day gain since July 31. Regional markets saw notable jumps, with Japan’s Nikkei rising 4.5%, South Korea’s KOSPI surging 7.5%, and Taiwanese shares leaping 9.1%.

The broader enthusiasm was fueled by Nvidia's own historic performance on Monday, when its shares surged 31.5% in their largest daily percentage gain in 23 years, restoring nearly $1 trillion in market value. This rebound eased lingering fears about slowing AI investments and moderating earnings growth, helping megacap tech concentration drive the Nasdaq 100 up by over 6%. Market watchers noted that Huang's return temporarily quieted anxiety surrounding the sector's reliance on the chipmaker.

Simultaneously, the sudden shift in sentiment altered macroeconomic expectations, loosening financial conditions and reviving market bets on near-term Federal Reserve tightening. According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, traders priced in a December rate hike as a certainty, contrasting with 89% odds previously recorded when stocks tumbled. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note climbed to 4.94%, while the 2-year note rose to 4.69%, and the dollar hovered near a 19-month high against the euro.

Commodity markets reacted differently as rising supplies from the Middle East drove oil prices down by more than 3% to near a three-month mark, with Brent crude settling near $89.50 a barrel. Meanwhile, spot gold recovered from a one-year low, climbing 0.7% to $3,657.97 per ounce as investors engaged in bargain hunting ahead of crucial US PCE Index data scheduled for release on Wednesday.

stories.title: حافظ آباد میں سابق وزیر مملکت لیاقت عباس بھٹی کے قتل کی منصوبہ بندی اور ملزمان کی گرفتاری
stories.summary:
پاکستان کے صوبے پنجاب کے شہر حافظ آباد میں سابق وزیر مملکت چوہدری لیاقت عباس بھٹی کے قتل کے الزام میں پولیس نے 11 ملزمان کے خلاف مقدمہ درج کر کے تین افراد کو گرفتار کرنے کا دعویٰ کیا ہے۔ آر پی او گوجرانوالہ خرم شہزاد وڑائچ کے مطابق ملزمان ایک ماہ سے اس قتل کی منصوبہ بندی کر رہے تھے اور ان کا مقصد لوٹا ہوا اسلحہ اور گاڑیاں بیچ کر افغانستان کے راستے بیرونِ ملک فرار ہونا تھا۔

مقدمے کے مدعی پنجاب اسمبلی کے رکن چوہدری ضمیر الحسن بھٹی ہیں۔ ایف آئی آر کے متن کے مطابق یہ واقعہ پیٹرول پمپ سے ملحقہ رہائش گاہ پر پیش آیا جہاں چار ذاتی محافظوں سمیت ملزمان نے لیاقت عباس بھٹی کو قتل کیا۔ پولیس نے بتایا کہ مقتول کو رسی سے پھندا دے کر قتل کیا گیا اور جائے وقوعہ سے چھری، رسی اور 19 دیگر ثبوت اکٹھے کیے گئے۔

پولیس کے مطابق ملزمان جاتے ہوئے دو کروڑ روپے سے زائد مالیت کا پچاس تولے سونا، بیس لاکھ روپے نقد، تین قیمتی گاڑیاں (پراڈو، ویگو ڈالا اور لینڈ کروزر)، اسلحہ اور گھر کا دیگر سامان لوٹ کر لے گئے۔ تفتیشی ٹیم نے گاڑیوں میں نصب سکیورٹی سسٹم کی مدد سے ملزمان کو ٹریس کیا اور خیبرپختونخوا کے علاقے ملاکنڈ سے تین اشتہاری ملزمان کو گرفتار کیا۔

آر پی او کا کہنا تھا کہ اگر لیاقت عباس بھٹی نے ملازمین رکھتے وقت ان کی پولیس ایپ پر رجسٹریشن کروائی ہوتی تو ان کا مجرمانہ ریکارڈ سامنے آ جاتا۔ مقتول لیاقت عباس بھٹی کا تعلق حافظ آباد کے سیاسی بھٹی خاندان سے تھا اور وہ 2002، 2008 اور 2013 میں مسلم لیگ ق کے ٹکٹ پر رکن قومی اسمبلی منتخب ہوئے تھے۔ اس کیس کے چوتھے نامزد ملزم کی گرفتاری کے لیے پولیس کی کارروائیاں جاری ہیں۔

stories.title: Pakistani Astronaut Zeeshan Ali Joins China's Shenzhou-24 Mission
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s Mohammad Zeeshan Ali has been officially named to the crew of China’s Shenzhou-24 space mission, which is scheduled to lift off on November 25 from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. Announced by the China Manned Space Agency, Ali will serve as a payload specialist during the mission, making him the first foreign national to board Beijing’s Tiangong space station. He will spend approximately a week in space performing experiments alongside Chinese crew members Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, before returning to Earth aboard the previously docked Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

The upcoming mission will involve executing roughly 90 scientific experiments, managing orbital rotation with the Shenzhou-23 crew, and conducting routine maintenance of the Chinese space outpost. High-ranking Pakistani officials, including Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, expressed immense national pride over the milestone, viewing it as a testament to the enduring friendship between Islamabad and Beijing. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif previously congratulated Ali and fellow trainee Khurram Daud in April, highlighting the cooperative space agreement signed between the SUPARCO and the CMSA in February 2025.

China has significantly expanded its space operations since being barred from the International Space Station by the United States in 2011, establishing independent orbital infrastructure and pursuing a goal of landing astronauts on the Moon by 2030. For Pakistan, a long-standing ally and major trading partner, participation in the Tiangong program marks a new dimension in bilateral scientific cooperation. Beijing continues to forge strategic partnerships globally to advance its ambitious space program while catching up to its main geopolitical rivals.

stories.title: Gold Prices Rise Slightly from Fourteen-Month Low Amid Bargain Buying
stories.summary:
Gold prices posted a modest gain on Tuesday, extending a recovery from a 14-month low as bargain hunters returned to the market following the previous week's heavy selloff. Spot gold rose 0.4% to $3,645.29 per ounce, whereas US gold futures for December delivery dipped 0.2% to $3,644.70. The slight recovery comes as traders carefully await upcoming US inflation data that could shape the Federal Reserve's monetary policy path moving forward.

The broader financial landscape remains sensitive to monetary tightening concerns. New York Fed President John Williams stated that persistently high inflation continues pointing the central bank toward tighter policy, though the exact pace of future rate increases will rely heavily on incoming economic figures. Attention is currently fixed on the US Personal Consumption Expenditures Index, a primary inflation indicator monitored closely as the central bank pursues its 2% target.

According to CME’s FedWatch tool, market participants are pricing in a 95% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the upcoming December policy meeting, with a larger 50-basis-point increase sitting at a 4.9% chance. Because higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, investors remain cautious about long-term positioning. Meanwhile, broader financial markets found strength after US stocks soared on Monday following news regarding Nvidia.

Other precious metals followed upward trends alongside gold during early trading hours. Spot silver climbed 1.2% to reach $43.55 per ounce, platinum advanced 0.4% to $1,330.42, and palladium recorded a 0.6% increase to settle at $898.95. Market participants continue to balance macroeconomic risks with currency and commodity adjustments.

stories.title: Pakistan Proposes Splitting Sui Gas Companies to Create Competitive Market
stories.summary:
The Pakistani government has finalised a reform framework to unbundle the country's two state-backed gas utilities—Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited and Sui Southern Gas Company Limited—into six to eight smaller independent corporate entities. Developed with technical assistance from the World Bank, KPMG, and Wood Mackenzie, the plan seeks to legally and operationally separate gas transmission, distribution, and sales operations. By dividing network transport from retail marketing, the government aims to eliminate conflicts of interest that previously allowed the companies to act as both monopolistic network operators and gas suppliers.

The reform framework has been submitted to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for in-principle clearance before seeking formal cabinet, parliamentary, or Council of Common Interests approval. The proposal enjoys backing from the International Monetary Fund as part of ongoing financial arrangements. As part of the restructuring, more than Rs3 trillion in accumulated gas circular debt would be transferred to a special purpose vehicle funded through a debt-servicing surcharge added to consumer tariffs. Officials estimate the transformation process will enter its implementation phase by the fourth quarter of 2027, requiring formal authorization within months.

Under the proposed model, the petroleum division intends to establish at least four gas sales entities, including two competitive gas supply firms for commercial and industrial users and two regulated entities for residential households. The Sui companies would be mandated to release 20% of their supply and consumer portfolios in the first year, followed by 10% in each of the subsequent years to foster private-sector competition. Financial modelling indicates that while transportation and competitive supply segments will be profitable from the outset, the domestic regulated supply sector will remain structurally loss-making due to tariffs falling far below cost-recovery levels.

To correct these fiscal imbalances, authorities plan to gradually raise domestic gas prices, reduce billing slabs from 12 to one, and deliver targeted subsidies to vulnerable protected consumers via social safety nets. Financial projections suggest severe deficits in residential segments, such as an anticipated after-tax loss of Rs158bn for SNGPL and Rs59bn for SSGCL under specific cost-allocation scenarios, necessitating substantial price adjustments. Furthermore, the plan estimates multi-year capital expenditure requirements of Rs736bn for SNGPL and Rs390bn for SSGCL through 2032 to modernize infrastructure and reduce network losses.

stories.title: Pakistan Moves to Unbundle Sui Gas Companies into Smaller Entities
stories.summary:
The government of Pakistan has finalized a comprehensive framework to break down the country's two major gas monopolies, Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) and Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL), into six to eight separate entities. Submitted to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for clearance, the plan aims to establish a competitive gas market by legally and operationally separating gas transmission and distribution from supply and marketing activities. Technical support for the restructuring was provided by the World Bank, KPMG, and Wood Mackenzie, with the International Monetary Fund also supporting the reforms.

The reform plan proposes creating at least four gas sales entities, divided into two competitive gas supply companies for commercial and industrial users and two regulated entities for domestic consumers. To foster competition, the Sui companies will be required to free up twenty percent of their supply portfolios for private participants in the first year, and ten percent in each of the subsequent two years. Financial projections indicate that while transportation and commercial segments will be profitable, the residential segment will incur losses due to heavily subsidized tariffs. Consequently, the government plans to gradually raise domestic gas prices, reduce billing slabs, and introduce direct subsidies for vulnerable households through a social safety net.

Additionally, over three trillion rupees in gas circular debt will be shifted to a special purpose vehicle funded by a consumer tariff surcharge. The restructuring also outlines massive capital expenditure requirements, including seven hundred thirty-six billion rupees for SNGPL and three hundred ninety billion rupees for SSGCL over several years to upgrade infrastructure and reduce system losses. Transaction advisers will be engaged to help implement the transition over the next five to six months, with the full rollout targeted for the fourth quarter of 2027.

This unbundling initiative matters because it addresses deep-seated financial distortions and structural inefficiencies within Pakistan's energy sector. By dismantling traditional monopolies and introducing market competition, the reforms seek to achieve long-term energy security, price rationality, and an investment-friendly economy while meeting critical international lending conditionalities.

stories.title: چنگیز خان کی زندگی، فتوحات اور دریائے سندھ کے کنارے جلال الدین سے جنگ
stories.summary:
تقریباً آٹھ سو سال پہلے تیموجن نامی منگول خانہ بدوش نے بحیرہ اسود سے بحرالکاہل تک ایک وسیع سلطنت قائم کی جو بعد میں چنگیز خان کے نام سے مشہور ہوا۔ ابتدائی زندگی غربت اور مشکلات میں گزارنے کے بعد اس نے چین، وسطی ایشیا، ایران، روس اور مشرقی یورپ کے حصوں پر حکومت قائم کی۔ مورخین کے مطابق اس کی سلطنت بارہ ملین مربع میل پر پھیلی ہوئی تھی۔

چنگیز خان نے کم عمر میں ہی اپنے سوتیلے بھائی کو قتل کر دیا تھا اور وہ اپنی عسکری حکمت عملی اور نفسیاتی مہارت کے لیے جانا جاتا تھا۔ اس نے اپنی زندگی خیموں اور میدانِ جنگ میں گزاری۔ فارسی مؤرخ منہاج السراج جوزجانی اور دیگر مورخین کے مطابق چنگیز خان ایک بے رحم اور ظالم حکمران تھا جو غداروں کو سخت سزائیں دیتا تھا، تاہم وہ اپنے نواسوں سے بہت پیار کرتا تھا اور بعض مواقع پر اس نے نرمی کا مظاہرہ بھی کیا۔

سنہ 1211 سے 1216 کے دوران چین کو فتح کرنے کے بعد وہ جلال الدین کا تعاقب کرتے ہوئے ہندوستان کی سرحد تک جا پہنچا۔ چنگیز خان اور جلال الدین کی افواج کے درمیان آخری معرکہ 24 نومبر کو دریائے سندھ کے کنارے ہوا۔ منگولوں کے گھیرے میں آنے پر جلال الدین نے اپنے گھوڑے سمیت 180 فٹ گہرے دریا میں چھلانگ لگا دی اور دوسرے کنارے پر پہنچ گیا۔

جلال الدین کی اس دلیری کو دیکھ کر چنگیز خان نے اسے نشانہ نہ بنانے کا حکم دیا، تاہم جلال کے اکثر سپاہی اور تمام بیٹے مارے گئے۔ جلال الدین وہاں سے دہلی گیا جہاں سلطان التمش نے اسے پناہ دینے سے انکار کر دیا، لیکن وہ ہندوستان میں ہی رہا یہاں تک کہ چنگیز خان نے اس کا پیچھا کرنے کا خیال ترک کر دیا۔

stories.title: قطری وزیراعظم اور امریکی وزیر خارجہ کی ملاقات سمیت پاکستان کی اہم خبراں
stories.summary:
قطر کے وزیراعظم محمد بن عبدالرحمان سے امریکی وزیر خارجہ مارکو روبیو نے ملاقات کی جس میں دوطرفہ تعلقات اور ڈائیلاگ کو آگے بڑھانے پر تبادلہ خیال کیا گیا۔ اس موقع پر قطری وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ نئے شعبوں میں تعاون کا مقصد دونوں ممالک کے مفادات اور امنگوں کو پورا کرنا ہے۔ اس اجلاس میں جوہری تحفظ کے نئے چیلنجز اور عالمی تعاون کے فروغ پر بھی بات چیت کی گئی۔

پاکستان کے حوالے سے مختلف خبروں میں بتایا گیا کہ پرتگالی وزیر خارجہ نے صدر مملکت آصف علی زرداری سے ملاقات کی، جس دوران صدر زرداری نے تجارت اور سرمایہ کاری کے لیے مشترکہ ورکنگ گروپ کے قیام کی تجویز دی۔ سندھ ہائی کورٹ نے نیب ترامیم کے بعد 50 کروڑ سے کم مالیت کے مقدمات سے متعلق 27 اپیلیں مسترد کر دیں۔ آئی جی سندھ جاوید عالم اوڈھو نے کراچی میں کاروکاری کے واقعات کو تشویشناک قرار دیا۔

پنجاب کی سطح پر وزیراعلیٰ مریم نواز نے صوبے میں پہلی مرتبہ جھینگوں کے جدید اور مربوط فارم ہاؤسز قائم کرنے کا اعلان کیا۔ مظفرگڑھ کے علاقے سیت پور میں ایک شخص نے تیز دھار آلے سے اپنی دو بیٹیوں کو قتل کرنے کے بعد خود کو اور بیوی کو زخمی کر دیا۔ حکومت کی جانب سے اگلے چوبیس گھنٹوں کے لیے پیٹرول سستا اور ڈیزل کی قیمت برقرار رکھنے کا نوٹیفیکیشن جاری کیا گیا۔

دیگر خبروں میں نیشنل سائبر کرائم انویسٹی گیشن ایجنسی نے لاہور سے سائبر ہراسانی اور بھتا خوری میں ملوث ملزم کو گرفتار کیا۔ اسلام آباد کی عدالت نے فاطمہ اصغر ہلاکت کیس میں کم عمر بچوں سے ملازمت کے قانون کی دفعہ لگانے کا حکم دیا۔ الیکشن کمیشن نے عائشہ گلالئی کی جماعت صفا کی چیئرپرسن ہونے کا نوٹیفیکیشن جاری کر دیا۔

stories.title: Pakistani Astronaut Zeeshan Ali Assigned to China’s Shenzhou-24 Space Mission
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s astronaut Mohammad Zeeshan Ali has been selected to join China’s upcoming Shenzhou-24 crewed space mission, which is scheduled to lift off on November 25. The announcement was made by the China Manned Space Agency. Zeeshan will serve as a payload specialist during the orbital mission and will return aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked with the Tiangong space station in May. The crewed spaceship is set to launch at 8:18 am Beijing Time from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi on a three-member mission.

During his expected one-week stay in space, Zeeshan will participate in conducting approximately 90 different experiments alongside the Chinese crew. His selection follows an agreement signed in February 2025 between Suparco and the China Manned Space Agency, which outlined training for two Pakistani astronauts in China. In April, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Zeeshan and fellow astronaut Khurram Daud after they were chosen for training, praising the milestone as a source of national pride that enhances bilateral ties.

The collaboration highlights close relations between Beijing and Islamabad, as China serves as Pakistan's largest trading partner and a major foreign investor. China has significantly advanced its space program in recent years, aiming to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030. Since being barred from the International Space Station in 2011 due to US legislative restrictions prohibiting NASA from collaborating with Chinese agencies, Beijing has increasingly built international partnerships, such as the cooperative agreement with Pakistan.

stories.title: Rawalpindi Police Submit Investigation Challan in Hina Javed Murder Case
stories.summary:
Police in Rawalpindi have officially submitted the challan for the murder case of 45-year-old Hina Javed to the District Prosecution Branch. The submission follows the completion of the investigation and the inclusion of forensic reports into the official case record. The district prosecutor has received the paperwork and initiated a formal scrutiny process.

Sources revealed that the initial investigation found no incriminating evidence against the victim's husband. Consequently, his name was placed in Column No II of the challan, leaving any further decisions regarding his status to the discretion of the court. The prosecution branch noted that if any legal deficiencies are identified during the review, the file may be returned to the police for rectification before being presented to the court of the district and sessions judge.

Hina Javed was murdered at her residence on August 20, leading to a murder case registered at the Civil Lines police station. The investigation has faced public scrutiny, as the victim's family previously expressed a lack of confidence in how police handled the inquiry. Civil society members have also held vigils to mourn her death.

The case has drawn significant public attention amidst various local reports concerning crime, safety perception indices, and judicial proceedings. The ongoing scrutiny remains a critical step before the matter is formally heard in the sessions court.

stories.title: Israeli Strikes in Gaza Kill UNRWA Worker and Two Others
stories.summary:
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza have resulted in the deaths of at least three people, including an employee of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees (UNRWA).
